candidates.name: Heads Down
candidates.one_liner: Put your Seeker face-down and it mines ORE. Pick it up and the rig goes cold. Proof of (actual) work.
candidates.concept: Heads Down is a focus-and-sleep ritual that turns the Seeker into an ORE rig that runs only while you are not using it. It builds products out of two unfinished promises: Solana Mobile's own 'Less scrolling. More seeking.' line and ORE's 'Proof of mobile: mine ORE on Seeker', which never shipped. You clock in from a Quick Settings tile placed beside Do Not Disturb, or by arming it and flipping the phone face-down. One Seed Vault double-tap puts a capped session budget into your own ORE Automation account, with Heads Down's DiscretionaryBps executor set as the executor. A foreground service fuses the phone's sensors and runs a tiny on-device classifier that tells a real pickup from a desk bump. While the phone is face-down, screen-off, or on the charger inside the night window, the executor deploys in every ~78 s round. When you unlock, a 'break' signal cools the rig after a 10 s grace, and the rest of the budget stays in an automation only you can withdraw from. There are three modes. Day Shift covers deep-work blocks, with an optional allow-list for calls, maps and music. Night Shift arms at bedtime on the charger, and the exact alarm is the clock-out that opens the overnight haul reveal. Stack is for friends at a table (found over Nearby/BLE) or in remote rooms: each posts an SKR bond, and the first phone to flinch forfeits it. You feel the rounds rather than watch them: a soft haptic thunk each round, a double thud on a winning tile, and an escalating pattern for a Motherlode. Meanwhile a Live Update chip reading 'Heads Down 1:12 · 55 rounds' sits on the lock screen and always-on display as a user-started session. Focus Rooms borrow Forest's Plant Together: the crew widget shows who is 'dark' right now, inverting social media's online dot, and in a strict room one pickup breaks the shift for everyone. The economics are honest by default. A live EV meter shows the expected cost per dark hour (production cost ~$104 against a ~$85 price). The default preset mines only when the Motherlode pushes rounds near break-even. A 'buying is cheaper today' banner, taken from STASH's mine-or-buy engine, appears when that is true. There are no emissions and no memo check-ins. One ShiftLog per shift, keyed to your SGT mint, makes streaks (with two automatic freezes) and a lifetime proof-of-focus record verifiable. Solo shifts use a Doze-proof break-signal model, where cheating only costs you your own SOL. Bonded Stack contests use Keystore P-256 heartbeats verified on-chain by the secp256r1 precompile, so SKR settles without trusting the team. Forfeited bonds can be swapped to ORE and buried ('your doomscrolling makes ORE scarcer'). Remove ORE and what is left is Forest for crypto people: weaker, but still a living habit. The founder story comes built in: 'I clocked 200+ build hours for Clock In with this app; my rig mined while I coded.'
candidates.daily_loop: TRIGGER: The morning alarm opens the Night Shift haul card, e.g. '312 rounds, 0.041 ORE, missed the Motherlode by one tile at 03:14'. The widget's 'rig heat' and the crew's dark-presence row prompt a work block, and Room or Stack invites arrive by push. ACTION: Usually zero taps: flip the phone or tap the QS tile, with one double-tap per session or a weekly refuel. The real action is not touching the phone. VARIABLE REWARD: A haptic every round, tile, solo-tile and Motherlode outcomes replayed at clock-out, rooms that complete or break, and Stack wins or losses. INVESTMENT: An SGT-keyed focus-hours ledger, a forgiving streak with auto-freezes, rig cosmetics that level up with hours (not spend), unclaimed ORE earning its refining-fee share, and standing rooms with your crew. WITHOUT AN AIRDROP: You work and sleep every day regardless, and this makes phone-down time feel productive. The ORE is a savings-flavoured variable reward, not points.

candidates.solana_integration: ORE program (oreV3EG1i9BEgiAJ8b177Z2S2rMarzak4NMv1kULvWv): one Automation account per user. Authority is the user's Seed Vault wallet; the executor is the Heads Down executor running the DiscretionaryBps strategy (e.g. 50 bps, disclosed in the UI; ORE caps it at 100). It sets a per-tile amount cap and native conditions (a min Motherlode for the Night Shift 'Motherlode hunter' preset, a max production cost), with reload and partial claims. ORE itself guarantees the executor can only deploy within caps or return funds to the authority, and the executor deploys only for rigs with a live shift. The Heads Down program (Pinocchio or Anchor) has five parts. (1) A Rig PDA [b'rig', sgt_mint], created only after in-program SGT verification: the Token-2022 account is owned by the signer with amount 1, TokenGroupMember.group == GT22s89nU4iWFkNXj1Bw6uYhJJWDRPpShHt4Bk8f99Te, and mint authority == GT2zuHVaZQYZSyQMgJPLzvkmyztfyXg2NJunqFp4p3A4, with a rebind when the SGT moves between the user's own wallets. It stores an attested Keystore P-256 pubkey that can sign shift and break messages but can never move funds. (2) A ShiftLog written once per shift (start, end, rounds, break reason). (3) Room PDAs with seats keyed by SGT mint. (4) A StackTable PDA with an SKR vault, settled permissionlessly from each participant's last secp256r1-verified heartbeat {table, slot, state=down}, read through instruction introspection against a checked instructions-sysvar address, with timeout refunds and pull claims. (5) A BuryVault plus a permissionless crank that swaps forfeited SKR to ORE via Jupiter and sends it to ORE's grams address. Hardened tier, taken from SHIFT: make the executor a program PDA whose permissionless crank CPIs into ORE deploy only when a fresh heartbeat bound to (program, shift, round id, counter) verifies, so no team key can deploy at all. It must be proven on a mainnet fork first; the fallback is a KMS-held executor key with tiny caps. Clock-in is one tx v1 that batches an optional Jupiter SKR/USDC→SOL swap, the Automation top-up and the rig update behind a single double-tap. The executor packs about 20 rigs' deploys into each 4 KB v1 transaction, since only authority, automation and miner are member-specific. Helius LaserStream and webhooks on the Board, Round and Miner accounts drive FCM pushes for the haptics, widget and Live Update. Why on-chain: custody stays in ORE's own Automation, seats and focus records must be sybil-resistant, and bonds between people must settle without trusting the team.
candidates.skr_role: Stack bond: friends escrow SKR in a StackTable PDA as the stake in a hardware-verified self-control contest, the same pattern that won MONOLITH's SKR prize for Seek. Settlement uses secp256r1-verified heartbeats, with timeout refunds and pull claims. An optional solo 'Doomscroll Tax' locks SKR on a declared shift; an early pickup swaps it to ORE and buries it. SKR works here as commitment collateral, not staking, not a reward and not a checkout currency; the word 'stake' should never appear in the UI. candidates.name: Night Shift
candidates.one_liner: ORE crews that follow the sun: whoever is on shift calls the dig for the whole crew, tiles are coordinated to cover the board, and an on-chain esusu pact shares the luck.
candidates.concept: Night Shift is a social ORE mining game for crews of 3-25 SGT-seated Seekers spread across time zones (Lagos, London, São Paulo, Seoul). It rests on one line: a mining pool is just an esusu for luck. Each member keeps their own non-custodial ORE Automation with a fixed daily budget and appoints the crew executor (DiscretionaryBps ≤100 bps, or a zero-fee mode on ORE's permissionless executor), so no pooled vault exists anywhere. The crew rig runs while someone is clocked in as foreman. The on-duty foreman makes 'the call' on a live 120 Hz heatmap (tile mask, per-round amount, Motherlode threshold, split/solo mix), and it is posted on-chain as a signed Call PDA. The executor may deploy only what matches the posted call and each member's own caps, so anyone can diff its deploys against the calls, which makes executor honesty publicly auditable. Within a call, the executor gives crewmates complementary tile masks, so the crew covers most of the board and lands on the winning tile far more often than any solo phone. Shifts hand off like a relay: 'tunde.skr clocked out, +0.42 ORE on his watch. You're up.' Budgets are fixed per day, so wider coverage means more exposure to a Motherlode that hits at a random hour, not more spend. Any sub can cover a missed shift, which works as a social streak freeze. The esusu pact is optional per crew. A chosen share of each member's mined ORE, read trustlessly from ORE Miner lifetime_rewards_ore deltas, is split every Sunday, so when Ji-woo's tile hits at 3 am Lagos time the whole crew eats. From the co-op design, each foreman gets an on-chain 'EV alpha' score: their calls measured against a uniform-allocation baseline computed from ORE's own round data. That lets Friday Crew Wars rank read-the-board skill rather than luck, with an on-chain trophy as the prize instead of a pot. Motherlode Watch pushes 'all hands' when the jackpot crosses a crew-set level, every crewmate's phone thuds in sync at each round reveal, and an auto-generated crew feed turns every call and outcome into a post with no posting burden. The app states plainly that coordination and pooling reduce variance but do not raise expected value (production cost ~$104 vs a ~$85 price), and it shows the expected cost per shift up front. The co-op lens's pooled, share-accounted vault is deliberately rejected: after ORE's June missing-account-check exploit, it is the highest-risk custody surface in the set. Why now: Automation plus DiscretionaryBps (Aug 17, 2026) made non-custodial third-party executors possible, the grid has ~150-165 miners per round and no social layer, and ORE's 'Proof of mobile' never shipped.
candidates.daily_loop: TRIGGER: The previous foreman's handoff push, the widget's 24-hour crew ring (who is on, next handoff), the morning card 'While you slept your crew mined 2.4 ORE · your share 0.19', and rare, urgent Motherlode Watch alarms. ACTION: Clock in from the QS tile or widget, one Seed Vault double-tap to sign today's call plus top-up, then a 10-second call on the heatmap; everything after runs hands-free. VARIABLE REWARD: A synced haptic reveal every ~78 s, your call's hit rate and EV alpha against every other foreman, solo-tile wins, Motherlode hits landing on your shift, crew reactions in the feed, and the Sunday pact split. INVESTMENT: A crew seat and coverage streak (subs cover gaps, two free gaps a month), your foreman record, crew banner and trophies, unrefined ORE earning refining-fee share, and pact history. WITHOUT AN AIRDROP: Your crew is counting on you to cover your time zone, and your call is on the record.

candidates.name: Whistle (the Seeker Swarm)
candidates.one_liner: Once a day the mine whistle blows at a random moment, and verified Seekers everywhere have three minutes to clock into the same ORE shift, spread across the whole board, so when a Motherlode lands the Swarm is on it.
candidates.concept: Whistle fuses BeReal's random daily prompt, Pokemon GO's community events and a mining pool, without the custody a mining pool normally needs. Every SGT-verified Seeker holds exactly one seat and keeps their own ORE Automation, with the Whistle executor as the DiscretionaryBps executor; no funds are pooled. Once per region per day, at an unannounced daytime moment, the whistle blows. Members then have 3 minutes to clock in with one double-tap that tops up that Rush's budget and writes a ClockIn attendance PDA in the same transaction. For the ~15-round Rush, the executor water-fills each member's stake across the board against other miners' live deployments. The Swarm covers all 25 tiles without members diluting each other; piling the crowd onto one tile would split a fixed per-round reward and be sharply -EV. Between Rushes, an opt-in 'Standing Swarm' mines only when the Motherlode is large (e.g. ≥200 ORE), where rounds approach break-even, and Motherlode Watch alarms pull everyone in when the jackpot crosses a threshold. When a big Motherlode hits, the Swarm is on the winning tile: members' .skr names light up on the board and every clocked-in phone buzzes in unison, a 'stadium buzz'. The headline metric is the Seeker Swarm's share of ORE's board. With ~150-165 miners and ~9-11.5 SOL per round today, 1,000 Seekers at 0.002 SOL per round would be roughly a sixth of it, a visible force on a top Solana protocol. It avoids the cold start that kills crew apps, because you need no friends who own Seekers: the whole Seeker base is your crew, with regional pride (Asia vs EMEA vs Americas shift boards) on top. Each Rush's captaincy is auctioned in SKR, and 100% of the winning bid is split among the seats that clocked in. The captain's banner rides on everyone's Live Update and widget, but their powers are limited to flavour (split/solo mix, Motherlode threshold). The UI keeps 'the Swarm won' separate from 'you won', because individual variance is not pooled. Budgets stay tiny and the message stays honest: a cheap ticket to a shared live event with real ORE, not yield. Why now: DiscretionaryBps executors (Aug 2026), 250 ms slots for late-round placement, tx v1 for batching ~20 member deploys per transaction, and ORE's never-shipped 'mine ORE on Seeker'.
candidates.daily_loop: TRIGGER: The whistle, once per region per day at a random time, as a heads-up plus a full-screen notification. ACTION: Tap the notification, go through the trampoline Activity and do one double-tap within 3 minutes (top-up plus attendance in one transaction), then glance at the Live Update chip. VARIABLE REWARD: Which rounds your tiles hit, the unison buzz at each resolution, the rare Motherlode caught by named Swarm members (maybe you), regional leaderboards and the Captain's banner. WITHOUT AN AIRDROP: Missing the whistle means missing the moment. That is BeReal's pull, backed by real stakes and a persistent community goal: the Swarm's share of ORE.

The Whistle program holds: a Seat PDA [b'seat', sgt_mint], created after on-chain SGT verification (TokenGroupMember.group == GT22s89…, mint authority == GT2zuH…, the signer's Token-2022 account holds 1); a Shift PDA (id, start slot, round range, captain, flavour, member count); and a ClockIn PDA [shift, seat], created in the same transaction as the Automation top-up so attendance is public and auditable. The executor is a Rust service on Helius LaserStream that reads the Board, Round and Treasury accounts. It computes a water-filling allocation against other miners' live deployments, deploys late in the round, and batches ~20 member deploys per tx v1 (member-specific accounts are only authority, automation and miner). Why on-chain: one-human-one-seat must be publicly verifiable, custody must stay with each member, and attendance and SKR splits must be auditable by anyone, including the ORE team checking usage milestones.

candidates.name: Foreman Tycoon
candidates.one_liner: Idle Miner Tycoon where the ore is real and the managers are real Seekers: hire a verified strategist to run your ORE rig overnight, and a Guard program makes it impossible for them to break the rules they advertised.
candidates.concept: Foreman Tycoon combines the idle-tycoon genre, a creator marketplace and ORE's DiscretionaryBps executor model. The mapping is exact: in Idle Miner Tycoon you hire managers to automate your shafts, and in ORE the third-party executor on your Automation is your manager, with its ≤1% fee as the manager's salary. You own a mine, which is your single ORE Automation (one per wallet), and you hire managers for shifts, such as a night-shift grinder or a Motherlode hunter. Managers are SGT-verified Seekers who publish immutable, versioned, declarative strategies: Motherlode minimum, per-round caps, tile-mask bounds, split/solo preference, time windows, max rounds per day and late crowd-aware placement. Your Automation's executor is the Foreman Guard PDA. A manager, or the hosted runner executing their strategy, calls Guard. Guard checks the contract, time window, caps and mask against live ORE board state, then CPIs ORE deploy via invoke_signed and splits the fee between manager and protocol. A manager therefore cannot deviate from what they advertised or touch principal, and 'Fire all managers' is one double-tap away from a tile or shortcut. The idle-game shell makes ORE's hard-to-follow mechanics readable. Shafts are shifts, the elevator is claims, the refinery is the refining-fee decision, the vault is stORE, tailings are buy-and-bury, and the offline-earnings screen is the real on-chain haul. Managers compete on a leaderboard of verifiable ORE-per-SOL over thousands of rounds. The co-op lens's on-chain EV-alpha metric is grafted in so skill is scored separately from Motherlode luck. The best strategists earn from many mines, which creates a creator class for ORE whose power users open the app daily and evangelize it. Mine dioramas level up only from real lifetime deploys, as cosmetics. Honest EV framing and Motherlode-conditioned strategies defuse the genre's 'get rich' promise. The Guard is published as an open, reusable least-privilege executor primitive that any ORE front-end could adopt, which is a public-good angle. Why now: DiscretionaryBps shipped Aug 17, 2026, ORE has no native mobile consumer app, and idle games are among the most proven 'come back tomorrow' formats.

VARIABLE REWARD: Haul size, Motherlode catches, managers climbing or falling the ranks, new strategies to try, and mine level-ups. INVESTMENT: Your mine's level and history, relationships with managers, and unclaimed ORE. On the supply side, managers are daily power users: they tune strategies, post shift notes and grow a following, because their fee income depends on verified performance. WITHOUT AN AIRDROP: A game loop over real hard-money accumulation for owners, and income for managers.

candidates.name: STASH
candidates.one_liner: Stack hard money the cheapest way: a one-tap daily save, plus optional spare-change round-ups, mines ORE when the board beats the market and buys ORE when it doesn't. SKR gifts arrive as live, SGT-locked miners.
candidates.concept: STASH is a daily hard-money savings ritual in the mould of Jar (daily digital gold), PiggyVest (autosave) and Acorns (round-ups). ORE is the asset, and the route to it is chosen for best execution. Each morning, 'Save today' is one Seed Vault signature on a single tx v1. That transaction tops up your own ORE Automation, set to mine only while the effective mining cost (including Motherlode EV) beats Jupiter's price, and swaps the rest into ORE at market. That makes STASH the one ORE app that tells you when not to mine, and a big Motherlode visibly makes mining cheaper. From Pickaxe comes an optional autopilot. It rounds up every swap, transfer or Solana Pay payment that Helius Parsed Streams detects and pulls the change through a capped Subscriptions & Allowances recurring delegation (e.g. ≤$3/day for 90 days). The change lands in a per-user stash PDA whose only exits are ORE deploys or the owner's wallet, with no signature per round-up. A weekly 'Sweep' packs a whole wallet clean-up into one 4 KB tx v1: SIMD-0437 excess-rent reclaim, closing empty token accounts and swapping dust, all sent to the board. The stash stays in your own ORE miner account and wallet. Unclaimed ORE earns a share of everyone else's 10% refining fee ('interest paid by people who withdraw'), and bought ORE can go into stORE. A 7 am dig report on the widget shows what the rig mined overnight, in ORE and in local currency (NGN, KRW, BRL, INR, PHP), next to a 'hard money vs your currency' chart that means more the longer you stay. Circles of 3-12 SGT-verified friends or family see each other's daily saves, with amounts optionally hidden. The streak is backed by a real value-moving transaction in the same tx, not a memo. 'Gift a Miner' turns SKR into a live, SGT-locked ORE rig for any .skr name: the SKR is swapped to SOL and escrowed against the recipient's SGT mint, so only a real Seeker can claim it, and it arrives pre-funded and already digging. It suits red envelopes, Eid gifts and Nigerian owambe 'spraying'. The founder story writes itself: the neighbourhood alajo sometimes vanishes with everyone's savings, and STASH has no collector. It is honest that under the hood it is a smart autominer plus DCA. It must frame ORE as a volatile 'hard-money sleeve', never a safe deposit. Why now: ORE's Automation conditions (max_production_cost, min/max Motherlode) shipped in Aug 2026, Allowances has been on mainnet since June, tx v1 and rent reduction just activated, and the official ORE app has been stale since Oct 2025.

candidates.name: MELT
candidates.one_liner: Every day the whole Seeker world prices one item (rice, petrol, a gigabyte), and each verified price tag earns an ORE mining shift. Together the reports build a phone-sourced, sybil-resistant street-price index quoted in local currency and in ORE.
candidates.concept: Crypto's founding story is fiat debasement, and much of the Seeker base lives it: Nigeria, Argentina, Turkey, Brazil, the Philippines. MELT is GasBuddy for the whole economy, paid in hard money. Each day one item drops for everyone (1 kg rice, 1 L petrol, 1 GB of data), and Seekers photograph its price tag on their commute. On the phone, ML Kit OCR reads the tag, faces are blurred and location is coarsened to an H3 cell. The capture digest is signed by an attested Keystore P-256 key and committed on-chain, one report per SGT per day. At 20:00 UTC every report reveals at once. Commit-reveal stops copying and creates a Wordle-style shared moment as per-city medians light up a global map ('rice in Lagos ₦2,450/kg, +38% YoY; in ORE, -12%'). Accepted reports are paid as ORE mining shifts. The MELT treasury runs rounds on the live board in each reporter's name, so reporters risk nothing and become ORE miners without ever buying SOL. Because losing-tile SOL recycles to the treasury, $1 of sponsor money funds roughly $9.50 of deploys. People who can't capture that day play 'Guess the Global Median', a Price Is Right mode. Flagged outliers go to SKR-bonded validators in a Schelling-point vote. Every price is also quoted in ORE, positioning ORE as the hard-money yardstick against melting fiat. The index is a public on-chain IndexFeed that programs, prediction markets and agents can read. Data buyers pay per query over Solana Payment Channels, which refills the wage treasury and buys ORE to bury. Reporter reputation (a quality-weighted wage multiplier), city coverage badges, a personal 'melt chart' of your own basket and a Sunday city CPI you helped build are the investment. Why now: ~121k SGT-verified devices make crowd data sybil-resistant for the first time, Payment Channels (Sept 3) make per-query data sales cheap, and the Foundation's stablecoin and internet-capital-markets push needs real-world price data. A web search found no phone-verified, crowdsourced street-price index on Solana.

INVESTMENT: Reporter reputation (wage multiplier), city coverage badges, a streak with freezes, your personal basket chart and the Sunday city CPI. WITHOUT AN AIRDROP: Still a GasBuddy/Numbeo-style utility plus a daily shared-object game (Wordle's reveal, Price Is Right's guess). Honest: this has the weakest organic retention in the set, and the wages carry much of the weight.

candidates.name: Gateman (Maigadi)
candidates.one_liner: Clock in with a float, not your vault: dApps get a capped daily allowance instead of your Seed Vault, every signature is explained and screened before the double-tap, and verified Seekers bond SKR to flag the scams.
candidates.concept: Drain fear is the loudest pain on r/SolanaSeeker, and the dApp Store has zero pre-sign or drainer-protection apps. Gateman (Maigadi, Hausa for the compound gateman) is a layered wallet defence built around the hackathon's theme: you clock in with a float, not your vault. Layer 1 is the Float. Each morning, or at the first dApp connect of the day, one Seed Vault double-tap grants today's device-bound day key a capped, expiring delegation from your vault through the audited Subscriptions & Allowances program (e.g. 25 USDC + 0.2 wSOL, expiring 23:59 local). Untrusted dApps connect to that key. A drainer can therefore take at most today's float. At night, or instantly from a lock-screen 'Clock out' tile, the float sweeps back to the vault and the allowance expires. Inside the cap, signing needs no Seed Vault prompt per transaction, so exploring gets faster and safer at the same time, and the float doubles as a degen's daily loss limit. Layer 2 is the Checkpoint, an opt-in Guard mode. Gateman registers as an MWA wallet endpoint and simulates each request with Helius. It renders a plain-English 'what leaves your wallet' card in your language via on-device LiteRT-LM (English, Pidgin, Yoruba, Portuguese, Korean, Japanese). It blocks structural drainer patterns: SetAuthority, System Assign, unlimited Approve, durable-nonce advances, lookalike recipients, programs upgraded in the last day, and signMessage payloads that are really transactions. Clean requests are then relayed to Seed Vault Wallet for the usual double-tap. Layer 3 is Caller ID. Helius streams on your wallets flag address-poisoning dust and phishing NFTs the moment they land ('lookalike of your contact bob.skr'), and 'Check with Gateman' appears in every app's text-selection menu, the share sheet and a QR-scan tile for Blinks and Solana Pay codes. Layer 4 is the Seeker Shield, an on-chain registry where SGT-verified hunters flag programs, mints and domains with an SKR bond. A flag auto-confirms when Helius observes a drain touching the target; otherwise it confirms after several independent seats agree and a 72-hour window passes unchallenged. Any wallet can read the registry over RPC or CPI. The daily layer comes from Clocked: a morning digest plus a one-double-tap tx v1 sweep that burns junk, closes accounts, revokes stale delegations and reclaims rent. 5% of the scam rent funds the hunter pool, so scammers pay the defenders. A 30-second daily 'Would you sign this?' puzzle renders a real drainer or decoy from yesterday exactly like a Seed Vault approval sheet, with a Wordle-style share grid. An evening Shift Report shows what was blocked and whether your flags were upheld, and a 'vault sealed' streak counts days your vault never touched an untrusted dApp. A Lockdown tile revokes every delegation and the float in one tx v1. Guard mode is deliberately optional, because MWA relay feasibility is the biggest unknown. The Float, Caller ID, select-to-check, sweep and puzzle all stand even if Seed Vault Wallet declines relayed requests. The pitch to the security judges is blast radius by construction, not better detection: even a fully compromised Gateman app can lose at most today's cap, because an audited program enforces the leash.
candidates.daily_loop: TRIGGER: Internal and already daily: 'I'm about to do my quests or try a new dApp.' A dApp's MWA connect routes to Gateman, which asks 'Clock in?'. Other triggers: the 8 am digest ('3 junk airdrops landed overnight, +0.006 SOL to sweep'), the numbered daily puzzle, and real-time heads-up alerts on new delegations. The widget reads 'Off the clock · vault sealed 63 days'. ACTION: One double-tap sets today's float, with zero per-tx prompts inside the cap. Then a 30-second puzzle and one double-tap to sweep, plus optionally flagging an unknown token or domain with a small bond. VARIABLE REWARD: Blocked-threat saves, rent recovered, puzzle result and streak, whether your bonded flags were upheld (bounty) or challenged, and the Friday Autopsy of the week's biggest caught drainer. INVESTMENT: The vault-sealed streak, personal allowlist and per-category float presets, hunter reputation keyed to your SGT mint, and the .skr contact graph that powers lookalike detection. WITHOUT AN AIRDROP: The fear is real, the found money is real, and the float is the explorer's fastest safe signing path.

candidates.solana_integration: Subscriptions & Allowances program (De1egAFMkMWZSN5rYXRj9CAdheBamobVNubTsi9avR44, audited): a fixed delegation per mint from the vault's Subscription Authority to today's day key, capped and expiring, with several mints granted in one tx v1 behind one double-tap. SOL for fees rides as wSOL and is unwrapped just in time, because the program is SPL/Token-2022 only. Gateman program (Pinocchio/Anchor): (1) a DayKey registry PDA [b'float', sgt_mint] binding vault ↔ current key ↔ expiry, so keys can be revoked or rotated and other wallets can recognize a leashed key; (2) Target and Flag PDAs [b'flag', target, sgt_mint], created only after in-program SGT verification (group GT22s89…, mint authority GT2zuH…, owner == signer, amount 1), holding the evidence hash and an SKR bond in a vault PDA; (3) a finalize path that auto-confirms on a submitted drain transaction signature touching the target within a window, otherwise uses optimistic multi-seat confirmation with a 72 h challenge and counter-bond, where the flagged dApp may dispute by signing with its program upgrade authority or dApp Store publisher key, escalating to an SGT jury or a timelocked security multisig; (4) a bounty pool PDA with pull claims, funded by 5% of swept scam rent and sponsors. Hygiene transactions: Token burn + CloseAccount for junk, Revoke for stale delegations, and WithdrawExcessLamports rent reclaim as SIMD-0437 steps land, batching dozens of accounts into one 4 KB v1 transaction. Analysis: Helius simulateTransaction, Parsed Events and Parsed Streams, DAS for spam metadata, and full parsing of v0 and v1 transactions, including AdvanceNonceAccount detection. Why on-chain: the leash must hold even if Gateman itself is compromised, and a public, bonded, sybil-resistant registry is a public good that Seed Vault Wallet or Phantom could consume.
candidates.skr_role: Hunter/truth bonds, a direct build of the SKR whitepaper's unbuilt 'Ecosystem Curators' for security. To flag a program, mint or domain as a drainer, a SGT-verified hunter posts an SKR bond with evidence. If the flag is upheld, the bond comes back with a share of the bounty pool (funded by 5% of swept scam rent plus sponsors) and hunter reputation; a false flag is slashed to the successful challenger or the disputing dApp. SKR becomes the price of making a public accusation. It is a claim-specific bond, never yield, not staking and not checkout. Avoid the word 'stake' everywhere.

candidates.name: Parachute
candidates.one_liner: A wallet guardian that fights back: when a drainer moves on your Seeker, a rescue you pre-signed with one double-tap pulls everything into your own 72-hour-timelocked vault in one atomic transaction, and one tap on the lock screen does the same under duress.
candidates.concept: Pre-sign scanners warn you before you sign, but many drains Seeker owners describe are 'smart trigger' drainers that use a delegate or authority granted earlier. Parachute covers what happens after the signature. Once a week the user 'packs' a parachute: one Seed Vault double-tap signs a durable-nonce tx v1 rescue transaction. It moves the full balance of every listed token account, and all SOL except fees, into the user's own Squads v4 vault, which has a 72-hour timelock the user's guardians can cancel. The signed rescue is stored encrypted on the phone (Keystore AES-GCM) and with Parachute's guardian service. Because it can only move your assets into your own vault, a leak loses nothing. A Helius LaserStream/Parsed Streams watcher runs detection rules on the wallet: a new Approve to a delegate outside the allowlist, a SetAuthority, outflows you didn't start, or contact with a drainer another Seeker has flagged. When a rule fires, the service broadcasts the rescue through Helius Sender with a Jito tip, racing the drainer on 250 ms slots. The durable nonce, the tool behind Drift's heist, becomes the defence. A lock-screen Quick Settings tile, 'Pull the cord', fires the same rescue without unlocking or opening Seed Vault. A thief or wrench attacker finds a timelock instead of a balance, and if the phone is taken, the owner can pull the cord from any browser with a passkey. A tiny stateless Pinocchio sweep_all program skips frozen or closed accounts so one failure never aborts the rescue. Custody reuses the audited Squads v4, so no new custody code is written. The daily layer is a rent-back and hygiene card (SIMD-0437 rent reclaim, closing empty accounts, revoking stale approvals in one tx v1) plus a herd-immunity feed. Every flagged drainer protects every Seeker through a shared, SGT-verified registry, which can be the same Seeker Shield as Gateman's. The business model is itself a Subscriptions & Allowances plan ($2.99/month in USDC, capped and revocable), so the product uses the safe pull pattern it recommends. If MWA's deprecated sign-only path is unavailable in Seed Vault Wallet, the fallback is a guardian role on a Squads/Swig policy account that can only sweep to the owner's own timelocked vault. It complements pre-sign scanners rather than duplicating them, and it aims to make Seeker the safest crypto phone, not just the one with a secure element.
candidates.daily_loop: TRIGGER: The shield widget ('Armed · covers 97% of $1,240 · packed 2d ago'), a push when a new asset arrives uncovered ('Repack: 1 tap'), and a morning herd feed ('3 Parachutes fired overnight; 1 new drainer flagged; you have 0 approvals to it'). ACTION: One tap clears today's hygiene card (reclaim rent, close empty accounts or revoke a stale delegate), or one double-tap repacks. VARIABLE REWARD: Real SOL recovered as rent reduction rolls out, a rising safety score, and occasionally a rescue that literally saves your money. INVESTMENT: A vault with guardians added by .skr name, a packed parachute, and reports that protect other Seekers. HONEST: The habit is insurance-shaped, weekly more than daily.

Android 16 Live Update while a rescue runs ('Rescue: 5/6 assets secured to Vault, unlocks in 72h'), a user-relevant in-flight session

ACTION_PROCESS_TEXT 'Check with Parachute' on any address in X or Telegram

candidates.solana_integration: The rescue is a tx v1 (4 KB) transaction using a durable nonce account whose nonce authority is the user; the larger size fits dozens of token accounts atomically without address lookup tables. A tiny stateless Pinocchio sweep_all program transfers each passed account's entire balance to the vault's token accounts, skips frozen or closed accounts and holds nothing. Custody reuses audited Squads v4: a time lock, spending limits for small instant withdrawals, and guardians added by .skr name. Detection runs on Helius LaserStream and Parsed Streams; broadcast goes through Helius Sender plus a Jito bundle, and 250 ms slots decide the race. A herd-immunity registry program lets SGT-verified devices flag addresses, one flag per SGT, verified in-program (group GT22s89…, mint authority GT2zuH…). The subscription is a Subscriptions & Allowances merchant Plan. Fallback if sign-only is unavailable: Squads/Swig policy accounts with a guardian role restricted to 'sweep to the owner's vault'. Why on-chain: the rescue must win an on-chain race, and the vault's timelock is what makes coercion pointless.

candidates.name: Punch
candidates.one_liner: Punch in on your Seeker and get paid by the second: each second worked is an escrowed, signed USDC voucher your phone verifies, ticking up on the lock screen and cashable at any moment.
candidates.concept: Punch is the literal 'Clock In' app: a time clock that pays, built on Solana Payment Channels (mainnet Sept 3, 2026, Cantina-audited), which no consumer mobile app uses yet. A payer opens a USDC channel to the worker once, escrowing for example a week of wages. The payer can be a DAO, a startup paying contractors, a shop or a client on any Solana wallet, no Seeker needed. The payer names a bounded voucher signer that can only ever pay that worker, and never more than the escrow. Long contracts refill themselves through a Subscriptions & Allowances recurring delegation, so the payer sets a weekly budget once and never signs again. The worker punches in with the Quick Settings tile plus a fingerprint; a Keystore P-256 key signs the punch, so no wallet popup appears. On site, they can instead tap an NTAG 424 DNA NFC tag (which resists cloning), scan a rotating QR code or enter a geofence. While the worker is punched in, cumulative 50-byte Ed25519 vouchers stream every few seconds, gated by device-signed heartbeats. The phone verifies each one against the on-chain escrow, even in airplane mode, so the number ticking up on the lock-screen Live Update is money, not a promise. The worker can settle mid-shift ('pay me now', earned-wage access on 250 ms slots) or let the week build up and settle once. One transaction settles thousands of vouchers, the operator pays the rent, and the worker never needs SOL. Non-payment risk shrinks to the last few seconds of work and the payer's risk is capped at the escrow. If a payer calls request_close, Helius streams trigger a high-priority push to settle before the grace period ends. Every punch is device-signed, keyed to the worker's SGT and anchored on-chain via the secp256r1 precompile in a daily Merkle-rolled ShiftLog. That yields a portable, verifiable work history for loans, visas and the next client, and rules out ghost workers. A payer-side widget shows the live roster and escrow burn, and distribute gives agencies and the platform a committed fee split, which is the business model. The first users are crypto contractors already in the Seeker base: moderators, community managers, designers, devs and QA across 57 countries, paid in USDC by invoice, late, and sometimes never. In Lagos, 30-60 day delays on crypto gigs are normal. The dApp Store has zero clock-in, shift or attendance apps, in a hackathon literally named Clock In: 'They named it Clock In. So we built the clock.'
candidates.daily_loop: TRIGGER: The workday itself: a morning nudge at your usual start time, arriving at the site's NFC tag, a payer's 'you're on today' push, and the widget showing today's contracts and this week's verified hours. ACTION: One tap on the QS tile plus a fingerprint, or tap the NFC tag; no wallet popup. VARIABLE REWARD: The lock-screen paycheck climbing with a soft haptic at each dollar, instant 'pay me now' cash-outs, and bonuses or tips that arrive as larger vouchers ('+5 USDC from ada.skr'). INVESTMENT: An on-chain verified-hours record and ratings tied to your SGT, recurring contracts that refill themselves, saved payer relationships, and a weekly Payday ritual where one Seed Vault double-tap settles everything. WITHOUT AN AIRDROP: It is your wage, and people open their pay app every workday.

Why on-chain: the escrow is non-custodial, the caps on the phone key are enforced by the program rather than a server, reputation is portable by device, and no website or regulator can quietly edit the rate index.
candidates.skr_role: SKR is the dispute layer. SGT-verified Seekers bond SKR to sit on a dispute panel. The losing party pays the arbitration fee in SKR, and jurors who vote against the final majority are slashed. Merchants can also escrow an SKR performance bond to unlock higher auto-release caps. This is program-held collateral, not the SKR staking program.
candidates.wow_demo_moment: Split screen, real phones, no cuts. Left: a friend's Android sends ₦25,000.37 through Moniepoint. Right: a Seeker lies face-down. The bank notification arrives, Alert's status-bar chip flips to 'Matched · ADAEZE O. · ₦25,000.37', the phone gives a haptic thump, and the escrow releases 16.10 USDC (Solscan tx on screen) before the sender has put their phone down. The left phone's widget shows the USDC landed. Voiceover: 'In Lagos we say alert don land. On Seeker, the alert IS the settlement.' Then someone sends a fake credit-alert SMS, and nothing happens: 'Unverified sender, ignored.'
candidates.closest_existing: P2P Protocol / p2p.me is the biggest direct competitor. It is live on Base, plans a Solana launch in Q3 2026, and supports UPI, PIX, QRIS and Nigeria, with ZK-KYC via Reclaim, staked merchants and on-chain disputes. Its merchants still confirm fiat receipt themselves, and it is web/Telegram-first and funded (a MetaDAO raise). Peer (formerly ZKP2P, Base) uses zkTLS proofs from Venmo, Revolut and Wise, which are rich-country rails. Binance/Bybit P2P, Noones and Yellow Card are custodial desks. Rampa (a 2025 BONK prize winner) does off-ramping, and PagCrypto handles BRL. The GitHub demo Osas-XLR8/crypto-escrow-p2p already sketches a PaymentNotificationListener. New here: a production Seeker app with program-capped hardware-key release via secp256r1, certificate-verified notification sources, SGT-keyed identity, Live Update merchant shifts and a public on-chain rate index.
candidates.technical_depth: A Rust program with about 12 instructions and LiteSVM/Mollusk tests, including adversarial cases: replayed P-256 signatures, a spoofed sysvar-instructions account, cap overflow, expired orders and a double-release race. A Kotlin/Compose app with a NotificationListener and a per-bank parser library, backed by a fixture corpus covering 20+ banks and fintechs in 4 countries, plus an on-device LLM fallback. The Keystore attestation chain is recorded for audit. A Kora fee relayer. A backend that does off-chain matching and turns Helius webhooks into FCM pushes, while settlement stays on-chain. THREAT_MODEL.md, and many granular commits across program, parser and app.
key_risks: Regulatory and personal legal exposure for a Nigerian founder: Nigeria SEC VASP rules, the 2024 Binance/naira episode in which executives were detained, and CBN pressure on AbokiFX over parallel rates. It needs non-custodial framing, geofencing and legal review
P2P Protocol may ship on Solana first, with funding and existing merchant liquidity
Payments funded by a third party (stolen bank accounts) can get the seller's bank account frozen; this is the #1 real P2P risk, and name matching only mitigates it
Bank notification formats change and some omit the payer's name, so the parser needs constant maintenance
The notification-access permission scares users and needs very careful onboarding
Two-sided liquidity cold start: merchants are needed in every currency

The demo needs real fiat transfers and several phones; Seeker ownership in Nigeria is unverified, and US-based judges may see it as regional unless the multi-rail design (PIX, UPI, M-Pesa) is shown working

dropped.name: Ajo (contrarian-founder-fit)
dropped.reason: Near-duplicate of Kin, a visible Clock In competitor repo that the brief lists under 'avoid near-duplicates'. Kin already ships bonded rotating circles, an in-program SGT check, delegation autopay, a jar-style widget and a 'Kin Score', and the ideator concedes Kin is 'very close on the basics'. Ajo's differentiators (a sealed-bid pot auction and a CPI-readable credit record keyed by SGT mint) are sub-features that add cognitive load and chit-fund regulatory exposure (regulated in India). On-chain ROSCAs date back to 2017 (WeTrust), and Ajo had the lowest self-scored innovation in the set (6). Parts that survive elsewhere: the 'alajo who vanished' founder story lives on in STASH, and the Allowances-pulled contribution pattern is covered in the cross-cutting insights.

cross_cutting_insights: Convergence map: 5 of 6 lenses proposed a drainer-protection or security product (all but prize-stacker-ore), which is the strongest convergence. 4 of 6 proposed the phone-down ORE rig (all but judge-whisperer and contrarian-founder-fit). ORE social mining appeared in 4 shapes across 4 lenses (relay crews, pooled co-op, swarm event, manager market). Punch came from 2 lenses and ORE savings from 2. The two strongest clusters sit on opposite sides of the rubric: ORE rigs are strong on habit, demo and meme but carry gambling optics, while security is strong on need, the store gap and judge fit but is insurance-shaped on stickiness.

The winning ideas share one primitive: a single foreground Seed Vault double-tap per day, session or week that moves real value and creates a bounded delegate to do the high-frequency work. That delegate is an ORE Automation executor, an Allowances delegation, a Payment Channel authorized_signer, or a Keystore P-256 key verified via secp256r1. This is both the answer to MWA's no-background-signing rule and the literal hackathon theme. Whatever wins should show the bound (cap, expiry, destination) in the UI and prove it in THREAT_MODEL.md.

In-program SGT verification keyed by SGT mint appears in essentially all 24 ideas: Token-2022 owner == signer, amount 1, TokenGroupMember.group GT22s89…, mint authority GT2zuH…, and rebind when the user moves it between their own wallets. Several ideas also claim it as the 'first public example'. Build it first as a standalone open-source crate with spoof tests (wrong group, wrong authority, zero balance, moved SGT). It is reusable across every candidate and makes a public-good story for Chase. It is not a differentiator, though, because other teams will ship one too.

Most ORE designs rest on an unverified assumption: that a program PDA can act as the ORE Automation executor or Miner authority via invoke_signed. SHIFT's heartbeat-gated crank, the co-op vault, the Tycoon Guard, the Night Shift pact, the STASH/Pickaxe autopilot, the STASH gift claim and MELT wages all depend on it. deploy.rs checks executor == signer, but first-deploy funding and system-account assumptions are unknown. Run a Surfpool mainnet-fork spike in week one. The safe fallback everywhere is a KMS-held executor key bounded by ORE's own deploy-or-return invariant plus per-round caps. Also, DiscretionaryBps automations cannot fall back to ORE's permissionless executor, so executor liveness is the team's job.

Minimizing custody wins with this panel (Toly's no-admin-keys ethos, Mert's 'admin keys are an illusion of comfort', Ethelsec, and the Radiants automated audit's 16 program-bug classes). Reuse audited or native custody (ORE Automation, Subscriptions & Allowances, Payment Channels, Squads v4) instead of writing pooled vaults. The one pooled-vault design (the FOREMAN co-op) was the riskiest code in the set, especially after ORE's June missing-account-check exploit, and was folded into Night Shift without its vault.

Honest ORE economics is table stakes. With production cost (~$104) above price (~$85), every ORE lens converged independently on a live EV meter, Motherlode-threshold defaults and tiny budgets. STASH's 'mine only when cheaper than buying, otherwise buy' engine is the strongest version and should be grafted into whichever ORE product wins: it pre-empts gambling optics and reads as anti-casino to Toly and Mert. Never call ORE mining yield.

The reveal anchors the daily loop and is the best demo beat. Options include a morning haul reveal via exact alarm (Heads Down, Night Shift, STASH, Pickaxe), a synchronized global reveal (Pulse at 9 pm, MELT at 20:00 UTC), a clock-out reveal (SHIFT), and an unannounced shared moment (Whistle). A scheduled, shared, variable-reward reveal is the most reusable retention mechanic in the set.

The native-surface stack converged: QS tile → translucent trampoline Activity → MWA; a Glance widget refreshed by Helius → FCM; composed haptics; ACTION_PROCESS_TEXT and share targets; App Shortcuts. Live Updates are allowed only for user-initiated sessions (shifts, calls, in-flight trades). Google forbids crypto price tickers and countdowns to future events, so an ORE round countdown or pre-whistle timer would violate the rules. Build for Android 15 with graceful degradation, because Seeker's Android 16/MR7 status is unconfirmed. Gate NFC at runtime with a QR fallback, since Seeker NFC is unconfirmed. Seeker's reportedly weak vibration motor threatens every haptic-hero demo, so test it early.

SKR converged on two non-staking patterns. (a) SKR as the stake in a hardware-verified commitment or skill contest (Heads Down Stack, SHIFT crew bonds, Night Shift reliability bonds, co-op EV-alpha duels), which mirrors Seek's MONOLITH SKR win. (b) Curator or truth bonds implementing the whitepaper's unbuilt 'Ecosystem Curators' (security registries, Pulse's question queue, MELT validators, Receipts reviewers). A common bridge in the ORE ideas: forfeited SKR is swapped to ORE and buried, which stacks both prizes. Always say bond or escrow, never stake. Fill the submission's free-text skrIntegration field explicitly, because the Align config may weight SKR at 20.

Hedge the Align AI criterion (20%) with an AI feature that does real work. Nearly every idea added an on-device LiteRT-LM model (Gemma 3 1B on CPU; Gemini Nano is not on Seeker). The most credible uses are security explanations in the user's language, private post-call language feedback and OCR, where on-device processing is itself the privacy feature (Mert sees AI's best crypto use in security). Decorative narration is the weakest use. The AI pre-screen reads the deck and the demo transcript, so narrate criterion-level claims plainly and never include instructions addressed to the reviewer, which are flagged to judges as a red flag.

Avoid memo spam. After the Aug 20 re-weighting, the daily on-chain action must carry value on its own (a top-up, a settle, a sweep, a vote with consequences). Log once per shift or day (ShiftLog, Merkle roll-ups, bitmaps) rather than per-minute check-ins, so usage reads as natural wallet activity.

Ethelsec and the Radiants audit expect the same security hygiene from every candidate. Check the instructions-sysvar address on any secp256r1 or Ed25519 introspection (the Wormhole class). Use SIWS with single-use server nonces. Show success only after confirmation with err==null, handling blockheight expiry and timeouts. Never write tokens or intent URIs to android.util.Log. Have no admin withdraw path, use a multisig + timelock (or revoked) upgrade authority, ship reproducible builds and fuzz/invariant tests, and write a THREAT_MODEL.md that bounds each hot key's worst case.

Founder stories converged: 7+ ideas draw on the builder's West African context (esusu/ajo, 'alert don land', the alajo who vanished, the maigadi gateman, 30-60 day contractor payment delays, naira debasement). MONOLITH winners had memorable founder stories. Use one that is literally true and tied to the product's mechanism, not decoration.

Verifiable traction beats claimed traction. ORE products produce on-chain metrics judges can check (miners added per round, SOL deployed, active rigs), and those same metrics map onto ORE's milestone-paid match. Payment products produce settled volume, and Pulse produces verified-respondent counts. Whichever candidate wins should put real testers on mainnet during the build month and show those numbers in the demo, and should build in public (the Cashflow precedent).

Many Seekers are drawer or second phones (SeekerTracker shows few daily-active primary wallets). Products that give a stationary Seeker a job (Heads Down's nightstand rig, Alert's merchant oracle, a Night Shift crew seat) or that live on the lock screen and widget fit that reality better than products that assume it is the user's main phone.

Shared infrastructure: Heads Down, Night Shift, Whistle and Foreman Tycoon share roughly 70% of their stack (the SGT crate, an ORE executor on LaserStream with tx v1 batching of ~20 deploys, Live Update/widget/haptics modules, a Codama ORE client). Gateman and Parachute share the Shield registry and hygiene sweep, and Punch and Airtime share the Kotlin voucher engine. The panel could pick one product and fold a sibling in as a mode (e.g. Heads Down rooms using Night Shift's auditable Call PDAs, or Whistle Rushes as a community event), but every extra mode adds executor load and dilutes the pitch.

Naming collisions across lenses (three 'Foreman', two 'Heads Down', two 'Punch') mean the chosen name must be checked against competitor repos and trademarks. Clock In theme wordplay (Punch, Shift, Night Shift, a 'Clock out' tile, 'clock in with a float') carries well with both the human judges and the AI pre-screen.
